GitHub renames release-asset filenames that have special or non-alphanumeric characters or leading/trailing periods. Uploading a same-named asset errors until the old one is deleted, hence --clobber and overwrite_files. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/assets#upload-a-release-asset

gh release create with assets makes a draft, uploads, then publishes, and the steps are not atomic. So published_at, which Obtainium's releaseDateAsVersion uses, is set after the upload, and the 'no dev release' window covers the whole upload. Source: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_release_create

'#' in a gh asset argument starts a display label, which is the likely reason behind Lawnchair's 'no # in filenames' comment. Source: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_release_upload ('append text starting with # after the file name')

Generated release notes list merged pull requests and contributors, so direct pushes to main produce nearly empty notes. Another reason to write SHA plus git-log notes yourself. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/automatically-generated-release-notes

Platform silent-update rule: on Android 16 (API 36) the updated app must target API 34 or higher, and 35 or higher on API 37. This is stricter than Obtainium's 'OS SDK minus 3' heuristic. Source: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/content/pm/PackageInstaller.SessionParams#setRequireUserAction(int)

Obtainium's Shizuku and root installers report canInstallSilently = true regardless of installer of record. This is a fallback if the first install did not come from Obtainium. Source: https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium/blob/fcd1807c8f8d2b8a5e27d4214ac4d472ed045598/lib/installers/shizuku_installer.dart

Alternative to the date pseudo-version: keep the rolling 'dev' tag but title each release with the versionName (e.g. 0.1.0-dev.123) and enable 'Use release title as version string'. The version then changes per build and can match the installed versionName. Source: https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium/blob/fcd1807c8f8d2b8a5e27d4214ac4d472ed045598/lib/app_sources/github.dart

On option C's 'rate-limit noise': Obtainium makes one /releases?per_page=100 call per check no matter how many releases exist (plus one more only if 'Verify the latest tag' is on). Per-build tags add clutter, not API calls. Source: https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium/blob/fcd1807c8f8d2b8a5e27d4214ac4d472ed045598/lib/app_sources/github.dart

Lawnchair precedent details: the nightly uses a separate applicationId (app.lawnchair.nightly), keeps the same versionCode on every nightly (16_00_02_01_00), and falls back to signingConfigs.debug when the secret keystore is missing (fork-safe). Its nightly job has no concurrency group. Source: https://github.com/LawnchairLauncher/lawnchair/blob/2d072998677ff198a0abc3f19c22af9ad32b5574/build.gradle

Obtainium's own release pipeline builds unsigned APKs in CI (uploaded as artifacts, draft release via ncipollo v1.21.0). The maintainer signs locally with apksigner and gpg-signs the sha256 (sign.sh), so the release key never reaches CI. Source: https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium/blob/fcd1807c8f8d2b8a5e27d4214ac4d472ed045598/sign.sh

APK Signature Scheme v3 key rotation (Android 9+, recommended above API 31) is the documented escape hatch if the dev or release signing key must change without a new package name. Source: https://source.android.com/docs/security/features/apksigning/v3

Developer verification: registering a new package name takes only the signing certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint. Private-key proof is required only for existing package names. Registering early is cheap, and so is squatting. Source: https://developer.android.com/developer-verification/guides/android-developer-console

The open-source-app-registration guide was last updated 2026-10-23, newer than the dates cited in delivery-36. Source: https://developer.android.com/developer-verification/guides/open-source-app-registration

Access note: the session proxy blocks api.github.com and github.com HTML for repositories outside the session, so release published_at dates and issue pages could not be read. Tag and commit dates came from git (git ls-remote and blobless clones) and file contents from raw.githubusercontent.com. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/actions/upload-artifact/cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9/README.md (example of a raw read that worked)
